Wait up to 1000 ms for voiceschanged and cache the pick per learner and locale.

Pre-generate audio for all fixed text (problem 'say', vetted hints, choices, narration segments, tutor and demo openings, demo-tutor lines) with /v1/text-to-speech/{voice}/with-timestamps on the chosen voice, using multilingual_v2 or a batch v3/v4 for best quality. Store the files with their alignment JSON under hash(text, voice, model, speed) on our CDN. Result: zero latency, the same voice as live replies, word timings for the glow, and nothing sent to a vendor for under-13 learners.

Tutor cursor spec: one 16 px rose dot with a 6 px soft halo, parked at the edge of the tutor caption or avatar. It glides center to center with transform: translate over clamp(220 + 0.35 × distance_px, 260, 650) ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1). It arrives 180 ± 50 ms before the anchored word's audio start (gaze leads speech), and then the existing ring blooms. The ring holds until the sentence ends + 400 ms, then fades while the dot stays. While the tutor is thinking, the dot drifts to the item under discussion and breathes (opacity 0.55↔1 every 1.6 s). While the learner talks, it moves to the mic or caption. Reduced motion: no glide, a 120 ms crossfade at the target on the word. Account for outputLatency in all timing.

Anchoring: the model writes an inline marker such as ⟦spot:practice.prompt.part.0.bottom⟧ immediately before the word it refers to. Parse it on the client (isSpotId, visibleSpots, guards), strip it from both the screen text and speakable, and record its spoken word index. When onBoundary reaches anchor index − lead, call spot(). Pointing then costs zero model round trips; drop point_at's server execute in voice mode. In typed mode, fire when the anchored word is revealed. Have hintSpot return the matched phrase so the demo tutor anchors on 'bottom' in 'the bottom number is 6'.

Barge-in: on Deepgram SpeechStarted, or mic level above −35 dBFS for 120 ms, while the tutor speaks and the input does not look like echo, duck TTS gain to 0.25 over 60 ms. If a non-backchannel word arrives within 700 ms, cancel with a 120 ms fade; otherwise restore over 250 ms. Targets: audible reaction ≤ 200 ms, fully stopped ≤ 800 ms. Truncate the tutor turn in the model context to the words actually heard, plus '[interrupted]'.

Turn-taking: K–2 done 1600 ms / open 2200 ms / hold 5000 ms, ignoring end punctuation the recognizer added, with Deepgram utterance_end_ms 1500. Grades 3–5: 1100 / 1800 / 4000. Grades 6–9: keep 700 / 1400 / 3000. Better: Deepgram Flux flux-general-multi (EN+ES) at wss://api.deepgram.com/v2/listen with eot_threshold 0.8 (K–5) or 0.7 (6–9), eot_timeout_ms 5000 (K–2) or 3000, and eager_eot_threshold 0.5 to start the LLM early, cancelling on TurnResumed. Send 80 ms frames (today's are about 43 ms). First check that Flux accepts the /v1/auth/grant token from the browser.

Latency budget, median on home Wi-Fi, logged per turn: end of turn ≤ 700 ms (6–9) or ≤ 1600 ms (K–2); first model text token ≤ 600 ms after the turn ends; first audio ≤ 300 ms after the first sentence completes. Total ≤ 1.6 s from the learner's last word to the tutor's first sound (6–9). Getting there needs answers checked in code before the model call and board tools with no server step.

Prompt voice-mode block, added when voice is on: at most 18 words per sentence, the question last, no parentheses, lists, tables, arrows or emoji, and math written in normal notation (3/4, 5 × 2 = 10) because the app speaks it. Remove 'say numbers the way you would say them aloud'.

Ship gates before calling it 'not uncanny': echo and self-interrupt test on MacBook speakers, iPad speakers (check whether iOS lowers playback volume while getUserMedia is open) and a Windows laptop. 20 real utterances per age band in each language, with no cut-off turns. Highlight drift ≤ 1 word at the end of a 60-word reply, tested on a recorded real ElevenLabs response. A blind listen of the 30-line script in which no listener picks out any line as robotic.
